newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends up but off highs on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends up but off highs on profit taking.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher but off their earlier highs as fund buying gave way to profit taking during the session's second half, traders said.
KCBT wheat had opened mixed, and nearby March chopped around early in two-sided trade on ideas that it closed too high relative to its CBOT counterpart.
But wheat gained at the midsession as fund-related buying entered the market and helped boost values, traders said.
Fundamental support came from news of impending tenders by Armenia and Lebanon.
One trader also cited talk suggesting Egypt may announce a tender for wheat later this week.

KCBT wheat closed steady to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/2 cents at $4.15-1/2 a bushel. July closed unchanged at $3.55, and a trader said the market seemed to have shrugged off concerns over possible winterkill damage to the crop.

Traders said Refco bought 2.2 million March and E D & F Man International bought 1.2 million March. CIS sold one million March and Prudential Securities had sold about 500,000 March and 700,000 May, sources said.
